Paramount+ Acquires Rights to Moonbug Series From the ‘Blippi’ and ‘CoComelon’ Universes (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago

“The Kelly Clarkson Show” went out with a bang. The daytime talk show won five awards at the 53rd Daytime Emmys on Friday, including the top daytime talk prize, the most of any program. Meanwhile, ABC’s “General Hospital” scored the top daytime drama prize (for the sixth consecutive year), winning four overall — tied with CBS’ newcomer “Beyond the Gates,” which also won four in its first year of eligibility.
This year’s Daytime Emmys came as a bittersweet moment for now-canceled talk shows “The Kelly Clarkson Show” and “Sherri.” “Sherri” host Sherri Shepherd won for daytime talk host, while “Kelly Clarkson” (besides best daytime talk) also won for directing for a daytime studio non-fiction series, hairstyling/makeup, art direction / set decoration / scenic design and sound mixing/editing. Because of the eligibility window, both shows will still be eligible for Daytime Emmys next year, as they produced original episodes in 2026. Among soaps, “Beyond the Gates” burst out of the gates in its first year with four wins, including for lead actress in a drama (Tamara Tunie, winning her first-ever Emmy), emerging talent in a daytime drama series (for Ambyr Michelle), lighting direction and hairstyling/makeup.
“This is the best ‘welcome back to daytime’ ever,” said Tunie, who first began working in the genre in 1987.
“General Hospital’s” four wins, beside daytime drama, also included victories for for writing team and for guest performer in a daytime drama (Jeff Kober, who also earned a Primetime Emmy nomination this year for “The Pitt,” a rare double nomination for both awards shows in the same year).
“Young and the Restless” won three, including supporting actor in a drama winner Roger Howarth (“The Young and the Restless”), who made Daytime Emmy history for the longest gap between wins (it’s been 32 years since he last won a Daytime Emmy). The show also won for supporting actress in a daytime drama (Beth Maitland).
In the first timers club, Star Jones won her first Daytime Emmy after 14 nominations — this time, in the daytime personality — daily category, for “Divorce Court.”
The Daytime Emmys recognizes daytime dramas, talk series, entertainment news, culinary, adventure, instructional and legal/courtroom programming — and for the 53rd edition, that covers an eligibility calendar of Jan. 1, 2025 to Dec. 31, 2025. This year’s Daytime Emmys nominations come after serveral rule changes were announced this spring .
“General Hospital” icon Genie Francis was this year’s Lifetime Achievement honoree, presented by her husband, actor Jonathan Frakes. “The joy of doing the work has never left me,” she said. “I am so proud to be a member of the cast of ‘General Hospital.’ The caliber of this cast inspires me every day and keeps me humble.”
Allen Media Group founder, chairman and CEO Byron Allen , host/executive producer Meredith Vieira , performer Patrika Darbo and actor/director/executive producer Francesca James are this year’s Gold Circle inductees, while Fox Television Stations exec VP of programming and development Stephen Brown and announcer/warm-up host Rubin Ervin are Silver Circle inductees.
There’s no host this year, but Matthew Hoffman served as announcer. Formerly held in June, the Daytime Emmys moved to mid-fall last year; the 2026 event took place as a single ceremony on Friday.
CBS led all outlets with eight wins for the network (its syndication arm CBS Media Ventures won an additional two). The now-defunct NBCUniversal Syndication unit won five awards thanks to “Kelly Clarkson.”
Here’s how the network/distribution tally went: CBS 8; NBCU Syndication 5; ABC 4; Inkblot 3
And the series tally: “Kelly Clarkson” 5; “General Hospital” 4; “Beyond the Gates” 4; “Young and the Restless” 3; “A Different Breed” 3
